answer: Trace-graph consistency scoring. Each agent action is signed with its cipher key and logged with timestamp and counterpart set; the detector builds a per-identity interaction graph and flags clusters whose edges appear before the identity’s first valid anchor event at the wharf registry. Enforcement: flagged clusters have payouts withheld pending manual review. Cost: an attacker must fabricate a plausible pre-history for every sock puppet, roughly 40 signed interactions each, making each fake identity cost about an hour of scripted activity rather than seconds.
